lab_title: The Human Heart: Anatomy and Blood Flow
top_level_objectives: Identify the four chambers, four valves, and major vessels of the human heart.
Trace the complete pathway of deoxygenated and oxygenated blood through the pulmonary and systemic circuits.
Explain the functional significance of myocardial thickness differences between the right and left ventricles.
Describe how heart valves function to prevent the backflow of blood during the cardiac cycle.

scenes.scene_name: Scene 1: External Anatomy and Major Vessels
scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the exterior of the heart and identify the major vessels entering and exiting.
key_visuals: A 3D beating heart model suspended in the center of the AR space.
Clearly demarcated superior and inferior vena cava, aorta, and pulmonary trunk with distinct textures.
student_actions: Rotate the heart 360 degrees to view it from all angles.
Select the major vessels to hear their names and read brief functional descriptions of where they transport blood.

scenes.scene_name: Scene 2: Internal Anatomy - The Four Chambers
scenes.brief_purpose: Reveal the internal structure to identify the right and left atria and ventricles.
key_visuals: A coronal cross-section of the heart displaying the four internal chambers.
Differentiated textures showing the inner walls, septa, and chordae tendineae.
student_actions: Tap each chamber to highlight it.
Read educational labels differentiating the receiving chambers (atria) from the pumping chambers (ventricles).

scenes.brief_purpose: Correlate the structural difference in the ventricular walls to their physiological roles.
key_visuals: A side-by-side highlighted view of the right ventricular wall and the left ventricular wall.
A visual caliper tool hovering over the myocardium to show scale.
student_actions: Measure the thickness of the right and left myocardium using the AR caliper.
Answer a multiple-choice prompt explaining why the left ventricle wall is substantially thicker due to systemic resistance.

scenes.scene_name: Scene 4: The Four Valves and Preventing Backflow
scenes.brief_purpose: Identify the tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral (bicuspid), and aortic valves and understand their roles.
key_visuals: A top-down surgeon's view of the heart with the atria removed.
Detailed 3D models of the four valves opening and closing in slow motion to demonstrate one-way flow.
student_actions: Pause the cardiac cycle to inspect the valves in their fully open and closed states.
Match each valve to its proper anatomical name using drag-and-drop AR text labels.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the path of deoxygenated blood from the body, through the right side of the heart, to the lungs.
key_visuals: Blue particle effects representing deoxygenated blood entering the right atrium and exiting the pulmonary arteries.
student_actions: Follow the blue particle path by sequentially selecting the vena cava, right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle, pulmonary valve, and pulmonary trunk.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the path of oxygenated blood returning from the lungs, through the left side of the heart, out to the body.
key_visuals: Red particle effects representing oxygenated blood entering via pulmonary veins and exiting the aorta.
student_actions: Guide the red particle flow by placing sequential waypoint markers in the left atrium, mitral valve, left ventricle, aortic valve, and aorta.

scenes.scene_name: Scene 7: The Complete Dual-Loop Cardiac Cycle
scenes.brief_purpose: Integrate both circuits to show simultaneous, dual-loop blood flow.
key_visuals: Fully animated 3D heart with synchronized blue and red particle flows.
Dynamic, real-time valve actions preventing backflow of the colored particles.
student_actions: Use an interactive slider to adjust the heart rate, observing how the two loops operate simultaneously without mixing.
Complete a final interactive sequence tracing a single drop of blood through the entire heart from vena cava to aorta.
